questions.q: What is an event handler in SSIS?
options: A workflow, built like a control flow, that runs in response to a run-time event raised by a package, container, or task
A T-SQL stored procedure that SSIS calls automatically on failure
A setting that disables logging for a specific task
A background Windows service that restarts failed packages
questions.explain: An event handler is a real workflow — with its own control flow and optional data flows — that SSIS runs when a specific event fires on a specific executable.

questions.q: Where do you build an event handler in SSIS Designer?
options: On the Event Handlers tab, using the same Toolbox and design surface style as Control Flow
In a separate stand-alone application outside of SSDT
Inside the Connection Managers panel
Event handlers can only be written in C# script, never dragged onto a surface
questions.explain: The Event Handlers tab is a full design surface — you drag the same tasks and containers onto it and wire them with precedence constraints, just like Control Flow.

questions.q: A task inside a Sequence container raises OnError, but neither the task nor the Sequence container has an OnError handler. What happens?
options: The event bubbles up to the next container in the hierarchy — in this case, the package — and runs its OnError handler if one exists
The event is silently discarded and no further container gets a chance to handle it
SSIS automatically creates a default handler that stops the package immediately
The task retries automatically up to three times before failing
questions.explain: Unhandled events escalate up the container hierarchy — task to container to package — until something handles them or the top of the tree is reached.

questions.q: Which event is the one most real-world packages actually build a handler for?
options: OnError — most often to send a failure notification
OnVariableValueChanged — to log every variable change
OnProgress — to display a progress bar to end users
OnPreValidate — to check credentials before every run
questions.explain: OnError is by far the most common event handler in production packages, typically wired to a Send Mail Task or a custom logging step.

questions.q: In the Event Handlers tab, what do the Executable and Event handler dropdowns control?
options: Which package/container/task the handler belongs to, and which of its events you're building a response for
Which SQL Server instance the package connects to
Whether the package runs in 32-bit or 64-bit mode
The order tasks execute in the Control Flow tab
questions.explain: Executable scopes the handler to a specific package, container, or task; Event handler picks which of that executable's events (OnError, OnWarning, etc.) you're responding to.
